findings.claim: `measures` requires `set(candidate) == {candidate_a, candidate_b}` to calculate candidate shares. In sections where either candidate receives zero votes, `candidate_a_share` is marked unavailable and `candidate_b_share` is omitted, causing all unanimous sections to be dropped from model training and evaluation.
findings.evidence:
```python
# election_audit/features.py:424-434
    if (
        unit["round"] == 2
        and candidate_a
        and candidate_b
        and candidate_a != candidate_b
        and set(candidate) == {candidate_a, candidate_b}
    ):
        a, b = candidate.get(candidate_a), candidate.get(candidate_b)
        denom = a + b if type(a) is int and type(b) is int else None
        for code, label in [(candidate_a, "candidate_a_share"), (candidate_b, "candidate_b_share")]:
```
When candidate 22 receives 0 votes:
`res = measures(unit, {"choices": {"13": {"count": 80}}, ...}, [], candidate_a="13", candidate_b="22")`
`candidate_a_share: (None, None, None, 'fixed_candidate_pair_required')`
`candidate_b_share: None`
findings.failure_scenario: In an indigenous or rural section where 100% of votes went to candidate 13 and 0 votes to candidate 22 (or an extreme stuffing anomaly), TSE BWEB omits candidate 22 from choices. `features.py` marks `candidate_a_share` unavailable with 'fixed_candidate_pair_required' and drops candidate_b_share. Downstream, `research_models.py` filters `WHERE readiness_state='ready'`, silently excluding the most extreme sections from the statistical models.
findings.falsification: Call `measures(unit, counts, [], candidate_a="13", candidate_b="22")` with counts containing only candidate 13 votes and verifying that `candidate_a_share` evaluates to 1.0 with readiness_state 'ready'.
findings.title: Unanimous and zero-vote sections are marked unavailable and excluded from candidate share targets

findings.claim: `perturb_mechanism` implements strictly one-directional fraud perturbations that only add votes to candidate A and subtract from B. Furthermore, `validate_mechanisms` hardcodes candidate numbers to "13" and "22", violating political neutrality and crashing on different candidate pairs.
findings.evidence:
```python

            if mechanism == "additions":
                q = min(q, row["electorate"] - row["a"] - row["b"] - row["other"])
                row["a"] += q
            elif mechanism == "switching":
                q = min(q, row["b"])
                row["b"] -= q
                row["a"] += q
            else:
                q = min(q, row["b"])
                row["b"] -= q
```
and
```python
# election_audit/research_models.py:884-886
                a, b = value("13"), value("22")
                if type(a) is not int or type(b) is not int:
```

findings.failure_scenario: An analyst running mechanism validation cannot simulate manipulation favoring Candidate B or victimization of Candidate A, because `perturb_mechanism` has no parameter to favor B. findings.claim: The scoring function `_score` assigns 0.0 to all observations inside the 95% prediction interval, tying 95% of units at tail rank 1.0. Furthermore, when the predicted interquartile range collapses to zero, dividing by `1e-06` explodes minor residual differences into massive outlier scores.
findings.evidence:
```python
# election_audit/research_models.py:163-165
    scale = np.maximum(p[:, 3] - p[:, 1], 1e-06)
    return np.maximum(np.maximum(p[:, 0] - values, values - p[:, 4]), 0) / scale
```
and
```python
# election_audit/research_models.py:401-402
            cal = np.asarray(model["calibration_scores"])
            rank = float((1 + np.sum(cal >= score)) / (len(cal) + 1))
```
findings.failure_scenario: In a normal calibration population, ~95% of sections have observations within `[p_0.025, p_0.975]`, receiving `score = 0.0` and `rank = 1.0`, destroying tail rank discrimination. In low-turnout or homogeneous sections where `p_0.75 == p_0.25`, a 0.01 deviation outside the interval produces a score of `0.01 / 1e-6 = 10,000.0`, dominating all other sections in triage purely due to precision artifacts.
findings.falsification: Evaluate `_score` with `values = 0.5` and `p = [[0.4, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.6]]`, producing 0.0, versus `values = 0.61`, producing 10000.0.
findings.title: Degenerate scoring function ties 95% of units at zero and blows up on quantile collapse

findings.claim: In `fit_models`, cross-validation splits folds by municipality using `GroupKFold`, but `DictVectorizer` is fitted inside each fold. Because municipalities in validation folds are held out, their municipality indicator features are out-of-vocabulary and silently dropped.
findings.evidence:
```python
# election_audit/research_models.py:214-226
            for ti, vi in GroupKFold(n_splits=3).split(contexts, y, groups):
                vec = DictVectorizer(sparse=True)
                x = vec.fit_transform([contexts[i] for i in ti])
                model = RandomForestQuantileRegressor(...)
                model.fit(x, y[ti])
                prediction = _predict(model, vec.transform([contexts[i] for i in vi]))
                losses.append(_loss(y[vi], prediction))
```
findings.failure_scenario: Hyperparameters are selected under an evaluation regime where municipality indicators are completely absent (all zeros in validation folds). When the selected tree depth and leaf size are applied to the full dataset, the model is trained with hundreds of municipality features active, creating an inconsistency between tuning and inference.

findings.title: GroupKFold across municipalities causes DictVectorizer to silently drop municipal features during tuning

summary: Review of Packet P7 (research design and statistics) identified 8 findings covering methodological bias, threat-to-validity, bugs, leakage, and unstated assumptions across `analysis-plan.md`, `features.py`, `research_protocol.py`, `research_models.py`, and `investigations.py`. Key issues include: (1) unanimous and zero-vote sections being marked unavailable and excluded from candidate share targets; (2) strictly asymmetric fraud injection and hardcoded candidate numbers 13 and 22 in mechanism validation; (3) degenerate scoring producing ~95% tied zero scores and catastrophic 1e-6 scale division on quantile collapse; (4) GroupKFold over municipalities silently zeroing out municipal features in DictVectorizer; (5) lack of mathematical specifications or implementations for confirmatory tests C1–C6 and BY correction; (6) omission of voter demographics inducing ecological confounding in test C5; (7) Phase 20b inspected sections outside Acre risking leakage into confirmatory partitions; and (8) outcome sensitivity assuming Candidate A won and failing to evaluate fraud favoring Candidate B.
